question: What effect does ocean acidification have on coral reefs and shell-forming organisms?

options.text: Ocean acidification has no effect on coral reefs.
Ocean acidification weakens coral skeletons and affects reef formation.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ocean acidification weakens coral skeletons and affects reef formation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ocean acidification weakens coral skeletons and affects reef formation.**
 
• Ocean acidification is caused by the absorption of excess atmospheric CO₂ by the ocean, leading to a decrease in pH levels.
 
• This reduction in pH affects the availability of carbonate ions, which are crucial for the formation of calcium carbonate structures in corals and shell-forming organisms.
 
• As a result, corals and shell-forming organisms find it harder to construct their skeletons and shells, making them more vulnerable to damage and erosion.
 
• Weaker coral skeletons lead to less robust reef structures, impacting the biodiversity and ecological balance of reef ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coral reefs** are vital marine ecosystems that provide habitat and shelter for many marine organisms.
 
• They also protect coastlines from the damaging effects of wave action and tropical storms.
 
• Ocean acidification, along with other stressors like rising sea temperatures and pollution, poses a significant threat to the health and sustainability of coral reefs worldwide.
 
• Conservation efforts and reducing CO₂ emissions are crucial to mitigate the impact of ocean acidification on these important ecosystems.
